claims: The Mariana Islands consist of the U.S. territory of Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI).
The Mariana Islands are a crescent-shaped archipelago of 15 volcanic mountains in the northwestern Pacific Ocean.
The capital is Saipan.
The population is concentrated on Saipan, Tinian, and Rota.
The Mariana Islands are situated south-southeast of Japan.
The Mariana Islands are situated west-northwest of Hawaii.
The southern islands including Saipan, Tinian, Rota are made of limestone with coral reefs.
The northern islands are volcanic.
The Mariana Islands have a tropical climate with a dry season from December to June and a rainy season from July to October.
The Mariana Islands are subject to typhoons, particularly between June and December.
Over 90% of the CNMI population resides on Saipan.
Northern Islands include active volcanoes on Anatahan, Pagan, and Agrihan.
The CNMI is an unincorporated territory of the United States in a political union.
English is the official language of the CNMI.
Chamorro and Carolinian are also spoken in the CNMI.
The currency of the CNMI is the United States Dollar.
Spain claimed the islands in 1565.
The U.S. military took control in 1945.
The CNMI entered into a covenant with the U.S. in the 1970s.
The Mariana Trench Marine National Monument protects submerged volcanoes and hydrothermal vents.
Saipan has the beaches of Micro Beach.
Saipan has the historical Last Command Post.
